newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn minister wants to let Germans be extradited.
newsitem.headline: Bonn minister wants to let Germans be extradited.

text.p: Bonn's Justice Ministry said on Friday it planned a constitutional reform to allow Germans suspected of crimes on foreign soil -- such as mercenaries in former Yugoslavia -- to be extradited to face trial abroad.
Currently the German constitution explicitly forbids the extradition of any German citizen.
But Justice Minister Edzard Schmidt-Jortzig told the daily Kieler Nachrichten it was "high time to eliminate national borders for criminal prosecutions".

His proposal, whose existence was confirmed by the ministry, would allow German citizens to be extradited to European Union countries and to international courts such as the war crimes tribunal on former Yugoslavia in The Hague.

The idea that a German mercenary could commit serious crimes in former Yugoslavia and then find shelter in his own country was "completely unacceptable, not only in foreign policy terms," Schmidt-Jortzig said.
